title: An acceptance evaluator child ran without termal_submit_acceptance_evaluation, so its verdict could not be recorded
outcome: An evaluator delegation spawned by termal_evaluate_acceptance always has termal_submit_acceptance_evaluation available before it starts judging. If the host cannot provide the tool (an MCP server that failed to start, a tool listing that timed out, a missing registration), the attempt fails as a host-side error before any judging, names the cause, and leaves the request retryable. It is not reported as an "insufficient-evidence" verdict by the evaluator. A test covers the missing-tool path, and the root cause of this field occurrence is diagnosed and recorded.
acceptance: A test drives a Codex evaluator child whose termal-delegation MCP server reports starting when its turn would begin. On unchanged master the turn starts without any readiness check (RED). After the fix the host re-polls readiness within the same budget as reviewers and starts the turn only once the server is connected and lists termal_submit_acceptance_evaluation.

If the server is not ready within the budget, or is connected without the submit tool, the evaluator attempt fails host-side before any model work, with a typed, recorded cause that is not an evaluator verdict and not the child's summary. A new termal_evaluate_acceptance request for the same work is then admitted. Tests show both cases.
An evaluator attempt that finishes with no recorded submission carries a host-assigned reason (no submission recorded) instead of presenting the child's own summary as its verdict. A test shows it.
Reviewer-mode readiness behaviour is unchanged; the existing reviewer MCP startup tests pass.
The root cause of the 02:17Z occurrence is recorded on this item with its evidence (the Codex log line and the transcript showing no termal-delegation tools).
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
